newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS-ING profits surge, cautious outlook.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-ING profits surge, cautious outlook.

text.p: Dutch financial services giant ING Groep NV (ING) reported a 25.4 percent leap in 1996 profits on Thursday despite hefty provisions and handed shareholders a more generous dividend than had been expected.

The banking and insurance group, which rescued the collapsed British merchant bank Barings in 1995, also said it would make a modest share placement in the United States but declined to make a profit forecast for 1997.
Analysts applauded the results, which were at the upper end of expectations, and ING shares were steady in Amsterdam, defying the downtrend in the Dutch market.
ING said net profit rose to a record 3.32 billion guilders ($1.8 billion) in 1996 from 2.65 billion in 1995.
It said almost all banking, insurance and investment activities reported considerably improved results as a result of a worlwide increase in total income.
"The strong results achieved in 1996 are in part a reflection of the favourable general economic trends in the countries in which ING operates," the group said.
ING said the consolidation of Barings and Poland's Bank Slaski contributed to a 33.7 percent jump in commission income and a 22.2 percent rise in operating spending.
But it made no other specific reference to the performance of Barings, which has been folded into its ING Barings investment banking unit.
The Dutch group said the excellent stock market climate also boosted commissions and was a factor in the 71.7 percent surge in securities trading income.

The increase came despite provisions of 530 million guilders before tax for future expenses, related partly to the cost of the introduction of a single European currency and computer and other changes for the millennium.
Pre-tax banking profit rose 21.7 percent to 2.13 billion guilders, while pre-tax insurance profit rose 18.6 percent to 2.50 billion guilders.
ING raised its dividend to 2.00 guilders per share from 1.66 in 1995, covered by earnings per share (EPS) which increased to 4.56 guilders from 3.84.
It also revealed previously hidden reserves of 2.55 billion guilders, which had to be disclosed in accordance with changes in European Union banking rules.
ING said it was full of confidence for 1997 and, barring unforeseen circumstances, looked forward to good results.
"However, despite a good start, the executive board considers it premature at this stage to make further profit forecasts," the group said.
ING said it would combine its listing on the New York Stock Exchange from the middle of June with a small placement of existing shares but this would not dilute EPS.
The 1996 net profit figure was at the upper end of analysts' forecasts of 3.17 billion to 3.36 billion guilders.
They were positive about the results and the increase in the dividend payout ratio.
"The absence of a clear profit forecast can be attributed to ING's usual caution, but with so much money put aside in provisions, there's quite a lot of room for 1997," said Heini Hakker of BZW.
Bart van der Feen of IRIS said: "All in all, these are very nice figures, with all components slightly better than expected."
At 1150 GMT, ING shares were steady at 70.30 guilders despite the Amsterdam AEX share index being down 0.42 percent.
